Porch Light
written for enough's verse fixtures, a villanelle (2026)

We keep the porch lamp burning through the night,
though every road beyond the gate is cold;
somebody walking home will need the light.

The moths come knocking, papery and white,
against the glass, as if they had been told
we keep the porch lamp burning through the night.

My mother did it, and her mother, quite
without a reason anyone could hold;
somebody walking home will need the light.

The neighbours think it wasteful, and they might
be right to say so, now the house is old;
we keep the porch lamp burning through the night.

It costs a little, and the bill is slight,
less than a coin, and worth as much as gold;
somebody walking home will need the light.

So when the wind comes up and stars are bright,
and all the dogs are sleeping in the fold,
we keep the porch lamp burning through the night;
somebody walking home will need the light.
